mainTopic: What each goat of ראש חודש, the רגלים and יום הכיפורים atones for, and the sources for the views of רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון
overview: This amud explains which sins the חטאת goats of ראש חודש, the רגלים and יום הכיפורים atone for. First the גמרא finishes explaining the view in which each goat has its own job. The festival goats are linked to the ראש חודש goats, so they atone for a matter of קודש. They cannot take over another goat's case, and every case with awareness is already covered, so they must atone for טומאה with no awareness at all. Next the גמרא looks for רבי מאיר's source that all the goats atone alike. It tries the extra ו of 'ושעיר', and then the פסוק 'אלה תעשו לה׳ במועדיכם' from רבי יונה. It also shows that ראש חודש is called a מועד. רבי יוחנן adds that even רבי מאיר keeps the inner goat of יום הכיפורים separate, and a ברייתא supports this. Finally the גמרא asks how רבי שמעון knows that each goat's job is locked in both directions, using the words 'עון', 'אותה' and 'אחת'. The amud ends as the גמרא begins answering whether 'אחת', written about the inner goat, can teach about the outer one. That answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Festival goats are compared to New Moon goats
steps.stepSummary: Through a היקש, the שעירי הרגלים are linked to the שעירי ראשי חדשים. Like the ראש חודש goat, the festival goats atone for a matter involving holy things.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the festival goats are compared to the New Moon goats. Just as the New Moon goat atones for something involving holy things, so too the festival goats atone for something involving holy things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a comparison (היקש) between the festival goats and the ראש חודש goats. This tells us that the festival goats also atone for some sin involving קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ראש חודש goat is already known to atone for a matter of קודש, meaning sacrificial food or the מקדש. The היקש moves that general category over to the festival goats. It does not yet say which exact case they cover, and that is what the next steps work out.

keyTerms.meaning: They were compared (by a היקש, a link made in the פסוק)
The חטאת goats brought on the festivals
The חטאת goats brought on ראש חודש
A matter involving holy things (sacrificial food or the מקדש)
They atone

steps.whyThisMatters: This היקש fixes the general category the festival goats belong to. Once we know they atone for a matter of קודש, the remaining steps can narrow down the exact case.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיתַּקּוּשׁ שְׂעִירֵי הָרְגָלִים לִשְׂעִירֵי רָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים;
phrases.english: And the goats of the festivals are compared to the goats of the New Moons;
just as the goat of the New Moon
atones for a matter involving holy things,
so too the goats of the festivals
atone for a matter involving holy things.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיתַּקּוּשׁ שְׂעִירֵי הָרְגָלִים לִשְׂעִירֵי רָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the derivation from the extra 'and' that the גמרא discussed just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The festival goats, like the ראש חודש goats, atone for a matter involving קודש.

steps.title: They cannot share the New Moon goat's job
steps.stepSummary: Someone might suggest that the festival goats atone for the same sin as the ראש חודש goat. That is rejected, because the פסוק says 'אותה', meaning only that goat bears that sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: let them atone for what the New Moon goat atones for. But we already said: 'it'. It bears that sin, and no other bears that sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible idea, that the festival goats cover the same case as the ראש חודש goat, and immediately knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אותה' in the פסוק about the ראש חודש goat was already read as exclusive. Only that goat atones for its particular sin. So the festival goats need a different case of קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (bringing up a possible idea)
But didn't we already say
'It' — a word read as limiting: only this one
Bears (atones for) sin

phrases.english: And if you would say:
let them atone for what the New Moon goat atones for —
but didn't we say:
"it" —
it bears the sin,
and no other bears the sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא נִיכַפְּרוּ אַדְּרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows down step 1 by ruling out the first possible case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the festival goats atone for the same case as the ראש חודש goat.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'אותה' makes the ראש חודש goat's atonement exclusive to it.

steps.title: They cannot share the יום הכיפורים goat's job
steps.stepSummary: Someone might suggest that the festival goats atone for the same case as the יום הכיפורים goat. That is rejected, because 'אחת בשנה' limits that atonement to once a year.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: let them atone for what the יום הכיפורים goat atones for. But we already said: 'once a year'. This atonement should be only once a year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second possible idea, that the festival goats cover the יום הכיפורים case, and rejects it as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The festivals come several times a year. If the festival goats atoned for the יום הכיפורים case, that atonement would happen more than once a year. The פסוק 'אחת בשנה' forbids that, so this option is also closed.

keyTerms.meaning: The Day of Atonement
Once a year
Atonement

phrases.english: And if you would say: let them atone for what the Yom Kippur goat atones for —
but didn't we say: "once a year" —
this atonement shall not be
anything but once a year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא נִיכַפְּרוּ אַדְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same pattern as step 2 to rule out the second possible case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the festival goats atone for the same case as the יום הכיפורים goat.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'אחת בשנה' limits that atonement to once a year, but the festivals come several times a year.

steps.title: So what else could they atone for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks, 'For what would they atone?' The question shows that only one case of קודש is left for the festival goats: טומאה with no awareness at the beginning or the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what else would they atone?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the argument with a rhetorical question. Both other options are ruled out, so the festival goats must cover the one remaining case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 showed that the festival goats atone for a matter of קודש. Steps 2 and 3 removed the ראש חודש case and the יום הכיפורים case. The next step goes through the remaining cases of awareness one by one and shows that each is already covered, which leaves only the case with no awareness at all.

keyTerms.meaning: For what / on what basis

steps.whatToRemember: The method here is elimination. The היקש puts the festival goats in the category of קודש, two פסוקים remove the other options, and the remaining case (no awareness at all) goes to the festival goats.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a real question asking for information. It is rhetorical: 'What else could they possibly atone for?' It proves the conclusion by showing that nothing else is left.

phrases.english: For what else would they atone?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי מְכַפְּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the elimination from steps 2 and 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Since the festival goats must atone for a matter of קודש and cannot take over the ראש חודש or יום הכיפורים cases, they atone for טומאה with no awareness at the beginning or the end.

steps.title: Each of the other cases is already covered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes through the three other cases of טומאה and shows that each one already has its own atonement, so the festival goats cannot be for any of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the festival goats atoned for a case where he knew at the beginning and at the end, that person brings a קרבן. If they atoned for a case where he knew at the beginning but not at the end, the inner goat of יום הכיפורים and the day itself hold off his punishment. If they atoned for a case where he did not know at the beginning but did know at the end, the outer goat of יום הכיפורים and the day itself atone for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering its own question from step 4 by crossing out the possible cases one at a time. Each case is shown to be already covered by something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are four ways awareness can go: knew at both points, knew only at the beginning, knew only at the end, or never knew. The first three already have an atonement: a קרבן, the inner goat, and the outer goat. Because steps 2 and 3 showed that the festival goats cannot take over another goat's job, these three cases are off the table.

keyTerms.meaning: Awareness. Knowing that one became טמא or that the food or place was holy.
At the beginning (before the sin) and at the end (after the sin).
Someone who is obligated to bring a קרבן.
The goat 'done inside.' This is the יום הכיפורים goat whose blood is brought into the קודש הקדשים.
The goat 'done outside.' This is the מוסף goat of יום הכיפורים, offered on the outer מזבח.
Suspends. It holds off the punishment until the person finds out, but it does not fully atone.

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the difference between תּוֹלֶה (holds off punishment) for the inner goat and מְכַפֵּר (fully atones) for the outer goat. These are not the same thing.

phrases.aramaic: אִי עַל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ יְדִיעָה בַּתְּחִלָּה
phrases.english: If they atone for a case where there was awareness at the beginning
and there was awareness at the end,
this person must bring a קרבן!

phrases.aramaic: אִי עַל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ יְדִיעָה בַּתְּחִלָּה
phrases.english: If they atone for a case where there was awareness at the beginning
but there was no awareness at the end,
for this, the goat that is done inside
and יום הכיפורים hold off the punishment!

phrases.aramaic: אִי עַל שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ יְדִיעָה בַּתְּחִלָּה
phrases.english: If they atone for a case where there was no awareness at the beginning
but there was awareness at the end,
for this, the goat that is done outside
and יום הכיפורים atone!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי עַל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ יְדִיעָה בַּתְּחִלָּה וְיֵשׁ בָּהּ יְדִיעָה בַּסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the elimination that the question in step 4 pointed to.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The three cases of טומאה that involve awareness at some point
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each of these cases already has its own atonement, so the festival goats would have no job there.

steps.title: Only the case with no awareness at all is left
steps.stepSummary: Since every other case is covered, the festival goats must atone for טומאה where he never knew, neither at the beginning nor at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: You are forced to say that they atone only for a case with no awareness, neither at the beginning nor at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the elimination. The festival goats atone for the one case left over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1 to 5 together show that the festival goats atone for something involving holy things, but not for any case another goat already covers. Only one case is left, so it must be theirs.

keyTerms.meaning: You are forced to say. Introduces a conclusion that has no other option.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, the רגלים goats atone for טומאה of the מקדש or its holy food when the person never knew at all, neither before nor after.

phrases.english: You are forced to say,
it atones only
for a case where there was no awareness
neither at the beginning nor at the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל כׇּרְחָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the elimination in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The festival goats atone for טומאה with no awareness at the beginning or the end.

steps.title: The משנה quotes רבי מאיר: all goats atone the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings up the opinion of רבי מאיר in the משנה: all the goats have the same atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: all the goats have the same atonement, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting רבי מאיר from the משנה. It is setting up a question about his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא explained a view where each goat has its own job. רבי מאיר disagrees: the goats of ראש חודש, the רגלים, and יום הכיפורים all atone for the same set of cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Their atonement is the same.
'Etc.' The rest of the quote from the משנה is not written out.

phrases.english: רבי מאיר says:
All the goats have the same atonement, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַשְּׂעִירִים כַּפָּרָתָן שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the view just explained, where each goat has its own job, to רבי מאיר's view that all the goats atone alike.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the goats atone for the same cases of טומאה involving the מקדש and its holy food.

steps.title: What is רבי מאיר's reason?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר רבי חנינא asks what source רבי מאיר uses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר רבי חנינא said: What is the reason of רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא בר רבי חנינא opens by asking for רבי מאיר's source. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge. It is a request for the פסוק behind רבי מאיר's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? A request for the source.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: רבי חמא בר רבי חנינא said:
What is the reason of רבי מאיר?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling quoted in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches all the goats share one atonement.

steps.title: The extra ו links all the goats
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק writes 'וּשְׂעִיר' instead of 'שְׂעִיר'. The extra ו links all the goats together, so they all atone alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק could have said 'a goat' but says 'and a goat.' This links all the goats to each other, because a ו adds onto the first topic.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא answers his own question. The letter ו in 'וּשְׂעִיר' ties each goat to the one before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ו means 'and,' so it attaches the new item to what came before. That makes a היקש among all the goats. Since they are all linked to the first one, the ראש חודש goat, they all share the same atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: They were compared or linked, as in a היקש.
A ו adds onto the first topic. It connects the new item to the earlier one.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's source is the ו of 'וּשְׂעִיר', which links all the goats so that they share one atonement.

phrases.english: The פסוק could have said 'a goat' but says 'and a goat,'
phrases.notes: This is about how the festival goats are written in במדבר 28–29.

phrases.english: so all the goats are linked to each other,
because a ו adds onto the first topic.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא ״שְׂעִיר״–״וּשְׂעִיר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra ו in 'וּשְׂעִיר' links all the goats together, so they all share one atonement.

steps.title: Can each goat learn from the one before it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the extra-ו source. If each goat learns from its neighbor, we get a chain of comparisons. But רבי יוחנן says that with קדשים, a law that was itself learned cannot be used to teach a further law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think each goat learns from the one next to it? But רבי יוחנן said that everywhere in the Torah we may learn from something that was itself learned, except for sacrifices, where we may not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 9. It shows that the extra ו seems to create a chain of learning, and a chain like that is not allowed for sacrifices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ו joins each goat to the goat listed just before it. So the פסח goat learns from ראש חודש, then the שבועות goat learns from פסח, and so on down the line. That makes each link a law learned from a law that was itself learned (למד מן הלמד), which רבי יוחנן says is forbidden for קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it enter your mind? (an opening that rejects an assumption)
Learning a law from a law that was itself learned
Sacrifices and holy matters
From its neighbor, the one next to it

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן's rule is not against learning from sacrifices in general. It only forbids a second-level chain, where the law doing the teaching was itself learned from somewhere else.

phrases.english: Does it enter your mind
that each and every one learns from its neighbor?!
phrases.notes: He means each goat learns from the goat listed just before it in the פרשה.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
In the entire Torah
we learn something learned from something learned,
except for sacrifices
where we do not learn something learned from something learned!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ כֹּל חַד וְחַד מֵחַבְרֵיהּ גָּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the extra-ו source from Step 9 actually works
steps.kashyaTarget: The extra-ו source for רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A chain of goats learning from each other is למד מן הלמד, which is not allowed in קדשים according to רבי יוחנן

steps.title: All the goats learn from the first goat
steps.stepSummary: There is no chain. Every goat learns directly from the first goat, the goat of ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is no problem. They all learn from the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from Step 10. It explains that every goat learns straight from the first goat, so nothing is learned from something that was itself learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ו connects its goat back to the original goat, the ראש חודש goat, and not to the goat just before it. That makes every comparison only one step from the source. So רבי יוחנן's rule against chains is never broken.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult
From the first one
They learn

phrases.english: This is not difficult,
they all learn from the first one.
phrases.notes: The first one is the ראש חודש goat, which is listed first in the פרשה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, כּוּלְּהוּ מִקַּמָּא גָּמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the structure of the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each goat learns from its neighbor, which makes a chain
steps.terutzMaskana: Every goat learns directly from the first goat, so there is no chain

steps.title: What about עצרת and יום הכפורים, which have no extra ו?
steps.stepSummary: The extra-ו source only covers goats that are written with 'ושעיר'. The goats of עצרת and יום הכפורים are not written that way, so how do we include them?
steps.simpleTranslation: That works for every goat where 'and a goat' is written. But for עצרת and יום הכפורים, where 'and a goat' is not written, how do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the extra-ו source. Some festival goats do not have the extra ו at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the letter ו in 'ושעיר'. For עצרת and יום הכפורים the פסוק says only 'שעיר', so the proof does not reach them. Yet רבי מאיר says all the goats are the same.

keyTerms.meaning: That works well (for part of the cases)
שבועות
From where do we know?

phrases.english: That works well for every one where 'and a goat' is written,
but Shavuot and Yom Kippur,
where 'and a goat' is not written, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח כֹּל דִּכְתִב בֵּיהּ וּשְׂעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the extra-ו source after Step 11 defended it
steps.kashyaTarget: The extra-ו source for רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source does not cover goats that are written without a ו, but רבי מאיר includes all the goats

steps.title: רבי יונה: the פסוק compares all the festivals
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה drops the extra-ו source. He learns from 'אלה תעשו לה׳ במועדיכם' that all the festivals are compared to each other, so all their goats atone alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יונה said: the פסוק says 'These you shall offer to ה׳ on your festivals.' All the festivals are compared to each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the extra-ו source and brings a new one from רבי יונה, which covers every festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' shows that the old source is being replaced. The closing פסוק of the festival sacrifices groups all the festivals together, which makes a הקש among them. That covers עצרת and יום הכפורים even without a ו.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (replacing the earlier answer)
They were compared (a הקש)
Festivals

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the new main source for רבי מאיר, and the next challenge is aimed at it.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yona said,
the verse says:
"These you shall offer to ה׳ on your festivals"

phrases.aramaic: הוּקְּשׁוּ כׇּל הַמּוֹעֲדִים כּוּלָּן זֶה לָזֶה.
phrases.english: all the festivals were compared to one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָה, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the extra-ו source because of the problem raised in Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new source replaces the old one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר's source is the extra ו in 'ושעיר'
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר's source is the הקש of all the festivals in 'אלה תעשו לה׳ במועדיכם'

steps.title: But ראש חודש is not a festival
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה's פסוק compares the festivals. But רבי מאיר also includes the ראש חודש goat, and ראש חודש is not called a festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: But ראש חודש is not a festival!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יונה's new source. A פסוק about festivals should not include ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says all the goats are the same, and that includes the ראש חודש goat. The word 'במועדיכם' only groups the festivals, so the ראש חודש goat seems to be left out.

keyTerms.meaning: The New Moon
A festival
But isn't it so that (opens a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ לָאו מוֹעֵד הוּא!
phrases.english: But Rosh Chodesh is not a festival!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ לָאו מוֹעֵד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יונה's source from Step 13
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הקש covers only festivals, but רבי מאיר includes the ראש חודש goat too, and ראש חודש is not a festival

steps.title: ראש חודש is also called a festival
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 14. ראש חודש is also called a מועד, as אביי shows from the פסוק 'קרא עלי מועד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: In truth, ראש חודש is also called a festival. This follows what אביי said: in that year, בית דין made תמוז a full thirty-day month. As it is written: 'He proclaimed a festival against me to crush my young men.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge that ראש חודש is not called a festival. It shows that ראש חודש is called a מועד after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in Step 14 assumed that רבי יונה's פסוק about festivals could not cover ראש חודש. אביי reads 'קרא עלי מועד' as speaking about an added day of ראש חודש, which the פסוק calls a מועד. So the ראש חודש goat is included in the comparison too.

keyTerms.meaning: In truth; actually (used to reject a challenge)
Festival; a set, appointed time
They made it full, a thirty-day month
The month before אב

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer protects רבי יונה's source. It lets one פסוק cover every goat that רבי מאיר includes, the ראש חודש goat as well.

phrases.aramaic: אִיבְרָא, רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ נָמֵי אִיקְּרִי מוֹעֵד,
phrases.english: In truth, ראש חודש is also called a festival,
as אביי says,
for אביי says:
Tammuz of that year,
phrases.notes: 'That year' is the year the people accepted the spies' bad report about ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: they made it full,
as it is written: "He proclaimed a festival against me
to crush my young men."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבְרָא, רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ נָמֵי אִיקְּרִי מוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the challenge's assumption is false: ראש חודש is called a מועד.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ראש חודש is never called a festival, so רבי יונה's פסוק cannot include its goat.
steps.terutzMaskana: A פסוק calls ראש חודש a מועד, so the ראש חודש goat is included with the festival goats.

steps.title: רבי מאיר agrees the inner goat is separate
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that רבי מאיר agrees the inner goat of יום הכפורים does not share atonement with the other goats in either direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבי מאיר agrees about the goat whose service is done inside the קודש הקדשים. It does not atone for what the other goats atone for, and they do not atone for what it atones for.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a limit to רבי מאיר's rule that all the goats atone alike. The inner goat of יום הכפורים is left out of that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, רבי מאיר said all the מוסף goats share one atonement. רבי יוחנן says this sharing stops at the inner goat. The exception works both ways: the inner goat cannot cover the others' cases, and the others cannot cover its case.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees (even though he might be expected to disagree)
The inner goat of יום הכפורים, whose blood is brought inside
The atonement the other goats give
The atonement this goat gives

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the inner goat has no role. It still works for its own case. It just does not swap cases with the other goats.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
And Rabbi Meir agrees
regarding the goat that is performed inside,
phrases.notes: This is the יום הכפורים goat whose blood the כהן גדול brings inside.

phrases.english: that it does not atone their atonement,
and they do not atone its atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the shared atonement of all the goats is established, the גמרא sets its limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even in רבי מאיר's view, the inner goat of יום הכפורים and the other goats do not share atonement in either direction.

steps.title: Why the exception works both ways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains both halves of רבי יוחנן's limit. The inner goat gives only one kind of atonement, and its atonement may happen only once a year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does it not atone for what they atone for? Because it gives one atonement, not two. Why do they not atone for what it atones for? Because the פסוק says 'once a year': this atonement may come only once a year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for each half of רבי יוחנן's statement. Both reasons come from the פסוק 'אחת בשנה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, 'one' teaches that the inner goat covers only one kind of case, so it cannot also take on the other goats' cases. Second, 'once a year' teaches that its special atonement happens only once a year. If the other goats could give that same atonement, it would happen many times a year.

keyTerms.meaning: One atonement, for one kind of case
Two atonements, for two different kinds of cases
Once a year (from the פסוק)

phrases.english: It does not atone their atonement,
because it atones one atonement
and does not atone two atonements.
They do not atone its atonement,
because the verse says, "once a year":
this atonement shall be
only once a year.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא אֵינוֹ מְכַפֵּר כַּפָּרָתָן – כַּפָּרָה אַחַת מְכַפֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasons behind each half of רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'One' limits the inner goat to one kind of case. 'Once a year' keeps its atonement from being given by the other goats.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבי יוחנן. It lists the cases that the festival goats, the ראש חודש goats and the outer goat atone for in רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this. For a case with no awareness at the beginning or at the end, for a case with no awareness at the beginning but awareness at the end, and for a pure person who ate impure קדשים: the goats of the festivals, the goats of ראשי חדשים, and the goat done outside all atone. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא to support רבי יוחנן's limit. This part lists the goats that share atonement, and it leaves out the inner goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts the festival goats, the ראש חודש goats and the outer goat of יום הכפורים together for the same three cases. The inner goat is missing from this list. That fits רבי יוחנן's claim that the inner goat stands apart, and the next step spells out what this omission proves.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this (support)
Awareness of the impurity
At the beginning and at the end
A pure person who ate impure sacrificial food
The outer goat of יום הכפורים, offered on the outer altar

steps.whatToRemember: In רבי מאיר's view, all the outer goats share one atonement. The festival goats, the ראש חודש goats and the outer יום הכפורים goat are all included. The inner goat of יום הכפורים is the exception.

phrases.english: It is also taught so in a ברייתא:
For a case that has no awareness,
phrases.notes: This means becoming impure and then entering the מקדש or eating קדשים.

phrases.english: neither at the beginning nor at the end,
and for a case that has no awareness at the beginning
but does have awareness at the end,
and for a pure person who ate impure sacrificial food,
the goats of the festivals and the goats of the New Moons
and the goat performed outside atone.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבי יוחנן's limit in Steps 16 and 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's statement that רבי מאיר keeps the inner goat separate from the other goats.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lists the shared cases of the festival goats, the ראש חודש goats and the outer goat, and leaves out the inner goat.

steps.title: The inner goat is left out of the list
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא never mentions the inner goat of יום הכפורים, and never mentions the case it atones for. This shows that, even for רבי מאיר, it does not share atonement with the other goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the goat whose service is done inside, he left out, and its atonement he also left out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what is missing from the ברייתא it just quoted. This finishes the proof for רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי מאיר lets the festival goats, the ראש חודש goats and the outer goat share each other's atonements. The inner goat is missing, and so is the case it atones for. So רבי מאיר keeps the inner goat apart, just as רבי יוחנן said in Step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: The goat of יום הכפורים whose blood is brought inside the קודש הקדשים (the inner goat)
He left it out
Its atonement, meaning the case that this goat atones for

steps.whatToRemember: Even רבי מאיר, who lets the goats share their atonements, keeps the inner goat of יום הכפורים completely separate.

phrases.english: But the goat whose service is done inside, he left out,
and its atonement he also left out.
phrases.notes: The printed גמרא says 'their atonement' in round brackets; the better reading in square brackets says 'its atonement'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ שָׂעִיר הַנַּעֲשֶׂה בִּפְנִים שַׁיְּירֵהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in Step 18
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן: the inner goat does not share atonement with the other goats.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's view in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of רבי שמעון's view: the ראש חודש goats atone for a pure person who ate impure קדשים. In his view each group of goats has its own job.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון would say: The goats of ראש חודש atone for a pure person who ate impure sacrificial food, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, the view of רבי שמעון. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rest of the משנה, shortened here as 'etc.', gives the festival goats and the יום הכפורים מוסף goat their own separate cases. Unlike רבי מאיר, רבי שמעון does not let the goats share. The גמרא will now look for the source of this.

keyTerms.meaning: The goats brought as חטאת on ראש חודש
They atone
A pure person who ate impure קדשים without knowing it

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon would say:
The goats of the New Moons atone

phrases.aramaic: עַל טָהוֹר שֶׁאָכַל אֶת הַטָּמֵא כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: for a pure person who ate impure [sacrificial food], etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי מאיר and opens the discussion of רבי שמעון's view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, each group of goats atones only for its own particular kind of case.

steps.title: Why can't the festival goats also atone for the ראש חודש case?
steps.stepSummary: We understand why the ראש חודש goat cannot take on the festival goats' case, since the word 'עון' limits it to one sin. But why can't the festival goats also atone for the ראש חודש case?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the ראש חודש goats do not atone for what the festival goats atone for, since the פסוק says 'sin', meaning it carries one sin and not two. But let the festival goats atone for what the ראש חודש goats atone for!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts one direction of רבי שמעון's rule from a פסוק. Then it challenges the other direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'עון' is about the ראש חודש goat, so it only stops that goat from carrying a second sin. Nothing yet stops the festival goats from carrying the ראש חודש sin as well. So the גמרא asks why רבי שמעון does not allow that.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It makes sense': the גמרא accepts one point before raising a problem
The festivals, here meaning the goats brought on the festivals
Sin, from the פסוק about the ראש חודש goat
Carries, meaning atones for

phrases.english: It makes sense that those of the New Moons
do not atone for what the Festival goats atone for,
since the verse says: 'sin',
meaning it carries one sin,
and does not carry two sins.
But let those of the Festivals atone for what the New Moon goats atone for!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּרָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים לָא מְכַפְּרִי אַדִּרְגָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source for רבי שמעון's separation of the goats
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's rule that the festival goats do not atone for the ראש חודש case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק 'עון' limits only the ראש חודש goat. Nothing stops the festival goats from also covering the ראש חודש case.

steps.title: The word 'אותה' keeps the ראש חודש case for its own goat
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'אותה', 'it'. Only this goat carries this sin, and no other goat does.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'it': it carries the sin, and no other carries the sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 21 with a second word from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עון' stops the ראש חודש goat from taking another sin. 'אותה' stops other goats from taking the ראש חודש sin. Together the two words lock the separation in both directions.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It': this goat alone
Another, meaning any other goat

phrases.english: The verse says: 'it',
phrases.notes: This is from the same פסוק as before: 'and He gave it to you to carry the sin'.

phrases.english: meaning it carries the sin,
and no other carries the sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא אוֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an extra word in the פסוק as a new source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the ראש חודש goat was limited, so the festival goats could also atone for its case
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אותה' makes the ראש חודש case belong only to the ראש חודש goat

steps.title: Why can't the יום הכפורים goat also atone for the festival case?
steps.stepSummary: We understand why the festival goats cannot take on the יום הכפורים case, since 'אחת בשנה' allows that atonement only once a year. But why can't the יום הכפורים goat also atone for the festival case?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the festival goats do not atone for what the יום הכפורים goat atones for, since the פסוק says 'once a year', meaning this atonement may happen only once a year. But let the יום הכפורים goat atone for what the festival goats atone for!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא runs the same pattern again, now with the festival goats and the יום הכפורים goat. It accepts one direction and challenges the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Once a year' means the יום הכפורים kind of atonement cannot also happen on the festivals. That limit only protects the יום הכפורים case. It does not stop the יום הכפורים goat from also covering the festival case, so the גמרא asks why not.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, the goat of יום הכפורים whose atonement רבי שמעון discusses
Once a year
Atonement

phrases.english: It makes sense that those of the Festivals do not atone
for what the Yom Kippur goat atones for,
since the verse says 'once a year',

phrases.aramaic: כַּפָּרָה זוֹ לֹא תְּהֵא אֶלָּא אַחַת בַּשָּׁנָה.
phrases.english: meaning this atonement should be only once a year.
But let those of Yom Kippur atone for what the Festival goats atone for!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא דִּרְגָלִים לָא מְכַפְּרִין אַדְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same kind of challenge, now for the festival goats and the יום הכפורים goat
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's rule that the יום הכפורים goat does not atone for the festival case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Once a year' only protects the יום הכפורים case from being repeated. It does not stop the יום הכפורים goat from covering a second case.

steps.title: The word 'אחת' allows only one atonement
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אחת' teaches that the יום הכפורים goat gives one atonement and not two. So it cannot also cover the festival case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'once': it brings one atonement, and does not bring two atonements.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 23 by reading the word 'אחת' in a second way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בשנה', 'a year', teaches that this atonement happens only once a year. 'אחת', 'one', teaches that the goat covers only one kind of case. So the separation works in both directions here too, just like in Step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: One or once: here it limits the goat to a single kind of atonement
Two atonements, meaning two different kinds of cases

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, each goat's job is locked in both directions. 'עון' and 'אותה' do this for the ראש חודש goat, and 'אחת בשנה' and 'אחת' do it for the יום הכפורים goat.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'once',
meaning it brings one atonement,
and does not bring two atonements.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא אַחַת כַּפָּרָה אַחַת מְכַפֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the word 'אחת' as a separate limit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the יום הכפורים case was protected, so the יום הכפורים goat could also cover the festival case
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אחת' limits the יום הכפורים goat to a single kind of atonement

steps.title: The word 'once' is written about the inner goat, not the outer one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 'אחת' is written about the inner יום הכפורים goat, so it cannot teach a rule about the outer goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the word 'אחת' (once) is written about the goat whose service is done inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from Step 24. The word 'אחת' comes from a פסוק about the inner goat, not the outer goat we are discussing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכפורים there are two goats. One has its blood brought inside, and the other is a מוסף offering brought outside. The פסוק 'אחת בשנה' speaks about the inside goat. So the גמרא asks how we can use that word to limit what the outside goat atones for.

keyTerms.meaning: But look! An opening word that signals a challenge.
When it is written
The goat whose service is done inside, meaning its blood is brought into the קודש הקדשים on יום הכפורים
That it is written

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two יום הכפורים goats. The inner goat has its blood brought inside. The outer goat is a מוסף offering. The question is whether a פסוק about the inner one can teach about the outer one.

phrases.english: But when it is written "once"
phrases.notes: This is the word 'אחת' from שמות 30:10, 'once a year', which Step 24 used as its proof.

phrases.english: it is written about the goat that is done inside!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כִּי כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source used in Step 24's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'אחת' to limit the outer יום הכפורים goat to one atonement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק with 'אחת' is about the inner goat, so it cannot set rules for the outer goat.

steps.title: A פסוק beginning 'aside from' links the two goats
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer by quoting a פסוק that starts with 'מלבד', meaning 'aside from'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Aside from...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by quoting a פסוק that begins with 'מלבד'. This is a setup line, and the rest of the פסוק and its point come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depends on a פסוק that mentions the outer goat 'aside from' the inner atonement offering. That wording ties the two goats together. If they are tied together, a rule written about the inner goat can also apply to the outer one.

keyTerms.meaning: Aside from, besides

phrases.english: The verse says: "Aside from
phrases.notes: This is במדבר 29:11, about the outer goat. The rest of the פסוק continues in the next part of the text.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering Step 25's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source link: a פסוק connects the outer goat to the inner goat
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A rule written about the inner goat has nothing to do with the outer goat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'מלבד' links the two goats, so a rule about one can apply to the other. The full point comes in the next part of the text.
